 Proposed SNAP rule change could threaten free school meal eligibility 
 Also in this week’s K-12 legislative update: Over 80 schools and organizations ask New York Governor Kathy Hochul for funding to expand kosher, halal, and plant-based meals in schools, and a Texas lawmaker introduces two bills ahead of the upcoming legislative session that would expand halal options in schools.
 Benita Gingerella , Executive Editor November 17, 2026
 3 Min Read According to the Food Research and Action Center, 6.3 million Americans who receive SNAP benefits would lose them if BBCE were eliminated. Photo: Shutterstock A proposed rule published by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) threatens to reduce Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) eligibility for certain individuals, which could impact the number of students who receive free meals at school. 
 At the state level this week, over 80 schools and organizations wrote a letter to New York Governor Kathy Hochul asking for funding to expand kosher, halal, and plant-based options in schools, and a Texas lawmaker introduced two bills ahead of the 2027 legislative session that would require school nutrition programs to provide halal meals upon request. 
 Here's the latest in school nutrition legislation. 
 USDA proposed rule threatens SNAP access for millions
 The USDA has published a proposed rule to eliminate the Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) under SNAP. 
 BBCE is a SNAP policy that states can opt into that extends SNAP eligibility to those who receive certain non-cash Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) or Maintenance of Effort-funded benefits. 
 Related: Aramark Student Nutrition partners with Chef Grace Ramirez to bring new recipes to Chicago Public Schools 
 If BBCE were eliminated, 6.3 million Americans who receive SNAP benefits would lose them, according to the Food Research and Action Center (FRAC ). This can have a lasting impact on school meal programs since children from families who participate in SNAP are automatically eligible to receive free meals in school. 
 In addition, it could reduce the number of schools and districts that participate in the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP), a federal program that allows schools and districts with high numbers of low-income students to provide all students with free school meals. CEP participants must reach a certain threshold of students who are considered low-income to participate in the program. If a CEP-participating school or district's number of low-income students decreases because their families no longer qualify for SNAP, the school or district may no longer qualify. 
 Schools and organizations ask for funding to expand kosher, halal, and plant-based options in New York schools
 Over 80 organizations and schools have sent a letter to New York Governor Kathy Hochul asking for funding to expand kosher, halal, and plant-based options in schools. The letter requests that $10 million be earmarked in the state's FY 2027-28 Executive Budget to establish voluntary opt-in grants to help school nutrition programs offer kosher, halal, and plant-based entrees and beverages. 
 The grants would be overseen by the New York State Education Department, and schools could use the funding for culinary training, consulting, technical assistance, menu development, food procurement, student engagement, halal and kosher certification, kitchen upgrades, and/or associated labor or operational expenses. 
 Related: New bill aims to ensure students have enough time to eat and play at school 
 Texas lawmaker wants to expand halal options in schools
 In a similar vein, Texas State Representative Suleman Lalani has introduced two bills ahead of the upcoming 2027 legislative session to require schools to provide halal options upon request. 
 Under HB401 , all school districts and open-enrollment charter schools in the state would be required to provide a halal meal to any student if they or their parent or guardian requests one, starting during the 2027-28 school year. 
 Under HB426 , only districts and charter schools located in or adjacent to a county that has a population of 2.1 million or more, would be required to provide a halal meal to a student if they or their parent or guardian requests one. This bill would also go into effect at the start of the 2027-28 school year.
